raw_case_text:
Here a 15-yr-old man, living in Tehran, Iran in 2015 was admitted to the reference hospital due to severe dyspnea, cough, prolonged fever, chronic diarrhea, shortness of breath and weight loss. The patient was hospitalized in Infectious Ward of a hospital in Tehran for further clinical and laboratory evaluations. Informed consent was taken from the patient.
He had bad taste in mouth, and milky lesions on the inner surface of the mouth. On the tongue and gums as well as candida lesions was observed. In addition, the patient complained of headache, body pain and severe fatigue. Furthermore, lymphadenopathy and adenoid has been reported in his history. HIV antibody test using ELISA kit (Arya Mabna Tashkis Company) was positive. RT-PCR was also used to confirm the result. The CD4 T cell count of this patient was about 300 cell/mul.
Nasal and oral swabs were taken from the aforementioned patient and cultured in the 1.5% non-nutrient agar (NNA) covered with a layer of heat-killed Escherichia coli in Page's solution. The plate was transferred to the Dept. of Parasitology and Mycology, School of Medicine, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran. The plate was then incubated at 30  C for to 2 months, and the cultures were checked every day using inverted microscopy. Acanthamoeba spp. was detected based on double walled cysts measuring 15 mu (Fig. 1) and flat shaped trophozoites with the unique acanthopodias. In order to achieve a plate without bacterial and fungal contamination several rounds of replicates was performed. Cloned amoebae was harvested from surface of the agar plate using sterile phosphate buffered saline (pH= 7). DNA was extracted using modified phenol-chloroform method. PCR reaction was performed using genus-specific primers pairs called JDP1 and JDP2, to amplify a fragment of approximately 500 bp region of the DF3 region in 18S rRNA gene. Sequencing of PCR product was performed by the Takapozist Company. To determine the genotypes, sequencing data was aligned with Acanthamoeba genotype sequences accessible in the GenBank database. The isolated strain belonged to Acathaomeba T4 genotype.
Moreover, thermo-tolerance and osmotolerance test was performed on the cloned strain. Briefly, thermo-tolerance was performed by incubating the strain in two different temperatures (37 and 40  C). For osmotolerance assay two plates, containing 0.5 and 1.5 M mannitol was prepared and cloned amoebae was passaged. Monitoring of the plates was done during 72 h. Interestingly, the isolated amoebae showed high pathogenic potential according the two mentioned tests.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 15-year-old male in Tehran, Iran, presented in 2015 with prolonged fever, severe dyspnea, cough, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, oral thrush, headache, generalized body pain, and severe fatigue.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The adolescent patient developed progressive constitutional, respiratory, and gastrointestinal symptoms including prolonged fever, cough, severe shortness of breath, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, dysgeusia (foul taste in the mouth), creamy white plaques on the oral mucosa, tongue, and gingiva, headache, myalgias, and severe fatigue, leading to hospitalization in the infectious diseases ward.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of lymphadenopathy and adenoid hypertrophy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prolonged fever, severe dyspnea, cough, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, foul oral taste, oral candidiasis, headache, body aches, and severe fatigue.

objective.physical_examination: Intraoral examination revealed milky white candidal plaques covering the inner buccal mucosa, tongue, and gingiva, accompanied by lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV antibody screening by ELISA (Arya Mabna Tashkis kit) was positive.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was approximately 300 cells/µL. Nasal and oral mucosal swabs cultured on 1.5% non-nutrient agar (NNA) overlaid with heat-killed Escherichia coli at 30 °C isolated free-living amoebae characterized by 15 µm double-walled cysts and flat trophozoites with acanthopodia, demonstrating high pathogenic potential via positive thermotolerance (growth at 37 °C and 40 °C) and osmotolerance (growth in 0.5 M and 1.5 M mannitol).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Oral and nasal mucosal colonization/infection by highly pathogenic Acanthamoeba genotype T4 alongside oral candidiasis in a 15-year-old male with newly confirmed HIV infection (confirmed by positive HIV ELISA, confirmatory HIV RT-PCR, and CD4+ T-cell count of ~300 cells/µL). Definitive amoebic identification was established by NNA culture, thermotolerance/osmotolerance pathogenicity assays, and PCR amplification (primers JDP1/JDP2) and sequencing of the ~500-bp DF3 region of the 18S rRNA gene confirming Acanthamoeba T4 genotype.
